sections.title: Imports for provenance notes
sections.what: Brings in the recipe and slide types and the citation type used to read each slide's citation data.

sections.name: provenanceNotes
sections.title: Building the provenance note text
sections.what: Creates the speaker-note text for a slide: a fixed statement that the note is recorded run evidence, followed by a structured block listing the claims, original wording, matching facts and projects, and any ids that could not be found.
sections.why: Stated in the comment: notes record evidence but never decide which claims are admitted.
sections.watch_out: Missing ids are listed rather than raised as errors, so a broken reference appears only inside the note text.

summary: Writes the speaker-note text that records where each slide's claims came from.
purpose: Lets the owner or a presenter check the recorded evidence behind any slide directly from its notes.
why: Stated in the comment: notes never decide which claims are admitted into the deck.
how: Collects the citations attached to the slide's title, subtitle, bullets, chart and footnotes, plus any source fact id stored in its metadata. It then looks up each fact and project in the recipe. The result is a short fixed statement followed by a JSON block with the run id, generation time, slide id, citations, original wording, the matching facts and projects, and lists of any ids that were not found.
inputs: The recipe result, one slide block, and the run id.
outputs: A single text string for the slide's speaker notes.
risks: Ids that cannot be found are listed rather than causing an error, so a broken link shows up only inside the notes. The note is labelled as recorded evidence, not fresh verification.
debug: If the notes are empty or missing facts, check that the slide's citations field is set and that the fact ids match those in the recipe. Look at the missingFactIds and missingProjectIds lists in the output first.
